classification.difficultyReason: The hardest diagrams require choosing intermediate angles across overlapping triangles, chaining triangle sums with straight-line or vertically opposite angles, and justifying each step.

content.prompt: Find α, β, γ or θ in each diagram below, giving reasons.

spec.description: Parallelogram with single arrows on AB and DC and double arrows on AD and BC.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel DC; AD parallel BC; angle A is 82 degrees; unknown interior angles D alpha, C beta, B gamma.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-82^\circ\\\alpha&=98^\circ\end{align*}$
Co-interior angles on parallel lines $AB$ and $DC$ are supplementary.
$\begin{align*}\gamma&=180^\circ-82^\circ\\\gamma&=98^\circ\\\beta&=180^\circ-98^\circ\\\beta&=82^\circ\end{align*}$
Use co-interior angles on parallel lines $AD$ and $BC$.

spec.description: Crossed triangles; A,C,E and B,C,D are collinear; matching single arrows mark AB parallel DE.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAC 55 degrees; angle DCE 85 degrees; alpha ACB; beta CDE.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=85^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles at $C$).
$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=180^\circ-55^\circ-85^\circ\\\angle ABC&=40^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles in $\triangle ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$\beta=40^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DE$).

spec.description: Four rays from B with a right-angle square between BE and BD.
spec.mathematics: Consecutive angles CBA 92 degrees, ABE 35 degrees, EBD 90 degrees and DBC alpha form a revolution.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\alpha&=360^\circ-92^\circ-35^\circ-90^\circ\\\alpha&=143^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC, horizontal AC extended right, and a ray from C parallel to AB with matching single arrows.
spec.mathematics: A 70 degrees; angle between CB and additional ray 30 degrees; alpha above extension, beta interior C, gamma interior B.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=70^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).
$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-70^\circ-30^\circ\\\beta&=80^\circ\end{align*}$
Adjacent angles on the straight line through $A$ and $C$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$\gamma=30^\circ$ (alternate angles on the parallel lines, with transversal $BC$).

spec.description: Triangle ABC formed by three extended straight lines QABT, SBCR and horizontal AC.
spec.mathematics: Exterior vertically opposite angles at A and C are 70 and 52 degrees; triangle angles beta, alpha, gamma.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=52^\circ$ and $\beta=70^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
$\begin{align*}\gamma&=180^\circ-52^\circ-70^\circ\\\gamma&=58^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles in $\triangle ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: A,O,P collinear; O,Q,B collinear; A,V,Q and P,V,B collinear. Curved callout leaders associate 24 degrees with OAQ, 92 degrees with AOB and 21 degrees with PBO.
spec.mathematics: Alpha OPB; beta OQA; theta PVA; gamma BVQ. No equality or parallel givens.

answer.short:
$\alpha=67^\circ$, $\beta=64^\circ$, $\gamma=43^\circ$, $\theta=43^\circ$.

Use triangle angle sums, a straight angle at $P$ and vertically opposite angles at $V$.
answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-92^\circ-21^\circ\\\alpha&=67^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles in $\triangle OPB$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-92^\circ-24^\circ\\\beta&=64^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles in $\triangle AOQ$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$\begin{align*}\angle APV&=180^\circ-67^\circ\\\angle APV&=113^\circ\end{align*}$
$A,P,O$ lie on a straight line.
$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-24^\circ-113^\circ\\\theta&=43^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles in $\triangle APV$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$\gamma=43^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles at $V$).

spec.description: Two extended parallel opposite sides with single arrows, the other pair with double arrows, and diagonal BA. All source point labels and six marked angles retained.
spec.mathematics: P,V,A,Q are collinear; R,B,C,S are collinear; VA parallel BC; VB parallel AC; angle RBV=88 degrees; angle BAC=49 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied 88° and 49° and unknown Greek labels are visible.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=49^\circ$ (alternate angles, $VB\parallel AC$).

$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-88^\circ-49^\circ\\\beta&=43^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles at $B$ lie on the straight line $RBC$.

$\gamma=88^\circ$ (alternate angles, $VA\parallel RB$).

$\theta=43^\circ$ (alternate angles, $VA\parallel BC$).

spec.description: Quadrilateral BCDA, preserving vertex order and all four interior-angle labels.
spec.mathematics: Interior angles B=55 degrees, C=88 degrees, A=68 degrees, D=alpha.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+55^\circ+88^\circ+68^\circ&=360^\circ\\\alpha+211^\circ&=360^\circ\\\alpha&=149^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with horizontal BC and a native drawn right-angle square at A.
spec.mathematics: Angle A=90 degrees; angle B=2 alpha; angle C=3 alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the right-angle mark and the two algebraic givens are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+3\alpha+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\5\alpha&=90^\circ\\\alpha&=18^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with AB extended beyond B and AC extended beyond C; exterior labels remain outside the corresponding vertices.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angles at B and C are 120 and 130 degrees; interior A=alpha and C=beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown alpha and beta remain unsolved.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-130^\circ\\\beta&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}\alpha+50^\circ&=120^\circ\\\alpha&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its opposite interior angles.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle PQR with one matching equality tick on each of PQ and PR.
spec.mathematics: PQ=PR; apex angle P=30 degrees; both base angles labelled alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: The two unknown base angles retain alpha labels.

answer.worked:
The base angles are equal because $PQ=PR$.

$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\alpha+30^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=150^\circ\\\alpha&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Triangle STU with horizontal SU extended beyond U, preserving the exterior-angle location.
spec.mathematics: Angle S=alpha; angle T=2 alpha; exterior angle at U=120 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived angle values are printed.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+2\alpha&=120^\circ\\3\alpha&=120^\circ\\\alpha&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its opposite interior angles.

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABCD, diagonal AC and AD extended beyond D. Single parallel arrows mark BC and AD. All source vertex and angle labels are retained.
spec.mathematics: BC parallel AD; ABC=108 degrees; CAD=40 degrees; ACD=71 degrees; BAC=alpha; exterior angle at D=beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angles and unknown symbols appear.

answer.worked:
$\angle BCA=40^\circ$ (alternate angles, $BC\parallel AD$).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-108^\circ-40^\circ\\\alpha&=32^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles in $\triangle ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=40^\circ+71^\circ\\\beta&=111^\circ\end{align*}$$
An exterior angle of $\triangle ACD$ equals the sum of its opposite interior angles.

spec.description: Two parallel rising oblique lines intersect a horizontal transversal. A falling diagonal passes through the right intersection. Unknown symbols occupy the original sectors.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding upper-right angles are 65 degrees; the falling diagonal makes 42 degrees with the rightward horizontal ray below it. Alpha is between the upper-left diagonal and upper-right oblique rays; beta is below-left between the horizontal and oblique rays.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown symbols appear.

answer.worked:
The upper-right angle at the right intersection is $65^\circ$ (corresponding angles, parallel lines). The upper-left angle between the diagonal and horizontal is $42^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-65^\circ-42^\circ\\\alpha&=73^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$. Also, $\beta=65^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).

spec.description: Intersecting triangles preserve A,P,O collinear; O,Q,B collinear; A,V,Q collinear; and P,V,B collinear. Alpha is angle PVQ, below V.
spec.mathematics: OAQ=22 degrees; AOB=60 degrees; PBO=25 degrees. No parallel or equality marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given angle measures and alpha are shown.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle OPB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle OPB&=180^\circ-60^\circ-25^\circ\\\angle OPB&=95^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $A,P,O$ are collinear, $\angle APV=180^\circ-95^\circ=85^\circ$.
In $\triangle APV$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVP&=180^\circ-22^\circ-85^\circ\\\angle AVP&=73^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $A,V,Q$ are collinear,
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-73^\circ\\\alpha&=107^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: P,A,B,Q and V,C,R,S lie on two parallel lines marked with double arrows. AC and BR have single matching arrows. BC is the internal joining segment.
spec.mathematics: VCA=75 degrees; CBR=35 degrees; BCR=alpha; BRS=beta. AC parallel BR and AB parallel CR.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied givens and unknown symbols appear.

answer.worked:
$\angle ACB=35^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AC\parallel BR$).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-75^\circ-35^\circ\\\alpha&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line $VCR$ sum to $180^\circ$.
Also, $\angle CRB=75^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AC\parallel BR$).
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-75^\circ\\\beta&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line $CRS$ sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Unlabelled triangle with a vertical altitude, right-angle square at its foot and base extended rightwards. No equality marks are added.
spec.mathematics: Right-hand small triangle has apex angle 30 degrees and perpendicular base angle 90 degrees; alpha is its right base interior angle and beta the adjacent exterior angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 30 degrees, the right-angle marker and unknown symbols appear.

answer.worked:
In the right-hand triangle,
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-90^\circ-30^\circ\\\alpha&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-60^\circ\\\beta&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$
Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
